signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.92, remaining beneath its falling SMA20/50/200 cluster spanning 157.55 to 158.53 with a downtrend structure in force. A 275bp policy differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) and a 267bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry premium structurally support the pair, but options pricing reflects sharp asymmetric downside demand. Saxo Bank 25d risk reversals sit at -2.24 with 1M ATM implied volatility at 7.8% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.9%, creating an elevated vol risk premium of +1.9%. Leveraged funds covered net short exposure by +12,222 contracts WoW to -25,598 contracts (pctl 94), showing speculative short reduction alongside heavy put demand. Carry dominance is directly constrained by options downside hedging ahead of this week's BoJ and FOMC decisions. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, positioning and options skew favor downside retest while below the 20-day moving average. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision on 30 Oct. Risk: Price clears the SMA20 at 157.87 and invalidates immediate downside momentum.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1225, holding below its downward-sloping SMA20 at 1.1238, SMA50 at 1.1440, and SMA200 at 1.1577 with a technical downtrend intact. The policy spread favors the dollar by 135bp (Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%), reinforced by a 146bp SOFR-€STR OIS advantage. Saxo Bank 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 6.7% versus 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, generating a notable +2.5% vol risk premium that signals heavy hedging demand over realized moves. Leveraged funds hold net short positioning of -94,138 contracts at the 2nd percentile of the 52-week range (z -1.72), indicating crowded short exposure prone to short-covering while BEER valuation registers cheap at z=-2.62σ. Downside momentum is structurally limited by extreme institutional positioning and elevated option hedging costs. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD, crowded short positioning caps clean downside continuation. Catalyst: ECB interest rate decision on 29 Oct. Risk: Sustained close below 1.1200 opens a fresh liquidation leg toward cycle lows.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Positioning + Retail Extreme Divergence
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.3160, trading beneath its SMA20 at 9.5030, SMA50 at 9.4110, and SMA200 at 9.5140 in a confirmed downtrend extended 2.38 ATR below its 20-day average. The policy rate differential offers a 50bp discount (Fed 4.00% vs Norges Bank 4.50%), favoring NOK carry while Norges Bank maintains an active tightening stance. Retail sentiment from Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 100% long positioning, directly opposing the pair's persistent spot downtrend. BEER valuation indicates spot is undervalued at z=-1.72σ against fair value at 9.4802, while Norway's ESI reflects steady outperformance at +14.0. The retail capitulation risk reinforces trend continuation lower as one-way retail longs remain trapped. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to retail extreme and aligned with carry deficit. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting on 5 Nov. Risk: Sharp oil price sell-off reversing NOK rate advantage and triggering retail squeeze.
